s:
Arrange the following approaches to monetary policy in India in chronological order:
A. Flexible inflation targeting with the MPC
B. Monetary targeting
C. Glide path associated with the Urjit Patel Committee and the 2015 Agreement
D. Multiple-indicator approach
x: Monetary targeting prevailed during 1985–1998, followed by the multiple-indicator approach during 1998–2014, the glide path during 2014–2016, and flexible inflation targeting from 2016 onwards.

sec: Monetary policy framework committees - chairperson + year (Urjit Patel, Chakravarty, Vaghul, Tarapore) [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Urjit Patel Committee’s recommendations?
o: Creation of a committee to decide policy rates
Adoption of CPI as the nominal anchor
A 4 per cent inflation target with a tolerance band of 2 percentage points
Continuation of the multiple-indicator approach as the sole framework

tq: Find the option that reverses the committee’s recommendation rather than merely changing a date or name.
sec: Monetary policy framework committees - chairperson + year (Urjit Patel, Chakravarty, Vaghul, Tarapore) [APPSC]

s: The multiple-indicator approach to monetary policy was criticised mainly because it:
o: made the RBI legally independent of the Central Government
required the MPC to meet only once every five years
excluded inflation from the policy framework
made market prediction difficult when different indicators gave conflicting signals
x: The approach was considered opaque because markets could not easily predict the RBI’s response when inflation, growth, exchange rate and credit indicators pointed in different directions.
tq: Link the criticism to its practical consequence for market predictability.
sec: Monetary policy framework committees - chairperson + year (Urjit Patel, Chakravarty, Vaghul, Tarapore) [APPSC]

s: Which of the following was identified as a challenge to monetary policy management in India after 1991?

To maximise economic growth irrespective of inflation

x: The flexible inflation-targeting framework uses a 4 per cent CPI-Combined target with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2 percentage points, namely 2 to 6 per cent.

x: All three statements correctly describe the division of responsibility: the Government sets the target, the RBI operates monetary policy to maintain it, and the RBI must explain prescribed failures.
tq: Separate target-setting responsibility from operational responsibility and accountability.

o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

s: The total strength of the Monetary Policy Committee is

o: The RBI Governor has two votes in every meeting.
Only the external members vote on the policy repo rate.
The Central Government can overrule a majority decision of the MPC.
Each member has one vote, and the Governor has a casting vote in case of a tie.

tq: Discriminate between an ordinary vote and a casting vote.

s: The external members of the Monetary Policy Committee are appointed for a term of
o: Four years and are not eligible for reappointment
Two years and are eligible for unlimited reappointment
Five years and are appointed by the RBI Central Board
Three years and are eligible for one reappointment

sec: MPC composition - members, appointment, casting vote, meetings, quorum

s: Which one of the following statements regarding MPC meetings is correct?
o: The MPC must meet every month without exception.
The MPC must meet at least four times a year and normally meets bi-monthly.
The MPC meets only when the Finance Ministry requests it.
The MPC must meet at least twice a year and normally meets quarterly.

tq: Separate the statutory minimum from the usual frequency of meetings.

o: Four external members, including the Government nominee
All six members of the Committee
Four members, including the Governor or, in his absence, the Deputy Governor
Three members, including the RBI Governor or Deputy Governor

o: Section 45T of the RBI Act, following the 2008 amendment
Article 280 of the Constitution, following the Finance Commission process
Section 45ZB of the RBI Act, following the 2016 amendment
Section 42 of the Banking Regulation Act, following the 1991 reforms
x: The MPC is a statutory body created under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act through the 2016 amendment.
tq: Use the exact statutory provision and amendment year as the deciding pair.

s: Which one of the following is a function of the Monetary Policy Committee?

It determines the annual allocation of Union Government expenditure.
It fixes the rupee-dollar exchange rate permanently.

s: Under Section 45ZN of the RBI Act, failure to meet the inflation target is deemed to occur when the average CPI inflation remains
o: above 4 per cent or below 2 per cent for four consecutive quarters
above 6 per cent or below 2 per cent for three consecutive quarters
above 6 per cent or below 2 per cent for three consecutive months
above 5 per cent or below 3 per cent for two consecutive quarters
x: Failure is defined as average CPI inflation remaining above 6 per cent or below 2 per cent for three consecutive quarters. The statutory wording refers to quarters, not months.
tq: Trap the month-versus-quarter confusion while retaining the correct inflation bands.

s: When the inflation target is missed in the statutory manner, the Reserve Bank of India is required to report to the Government the
o: exchange-rate level it will maintain for the next financial year
reasons for failure, remedial actions and estimated time to return to the target
names of all MPC members and their individual salaries
future Union Budget allocations and tax rates
x: The RBI must report the reasons for the failure, the remedial actions proposed and the period within which inflation is expected to return to the target.
tq: Ask what the responsible institution must do after a statutory failure.
sec: Failure to meet the target - consecutive quarters rule

s: Which one of the following is the primary objective of monetary policy under the flexible inflation-targeting framework?

Fixing the rupee-dollar rate — Monetary Policy Committee

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the roles of the RBI and the Finance Ministry in the monetary-policy framework?
o: The RBI sets all tax rates, while the Finance Ministry fixes the repo rate.
The Finance Ministry frames monetary policy, while the RBI only implements fiscal policy.

s: Which one of the following correctly compares the flexibility of fiscal and monetary policy?
